'''Adam Michael Flagler''' (born December 1, 1999) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Sacramento Kings]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA), on a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Stockton Kings]] of the [[NBA G League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Presbyterian Blue Hose men's basketball|Presbyterian Blue Hose]] and the [[Baylor Bears men's basketball|Baylor Bears]]. Flagler was a member of the Bear's [[2020–21 Baylor Bears basketball team|2021 March Madness championship]]-winning team and with the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]]'s [[List of NBA champions|2025 NBA championship]]-winning team.

==High school career==
Flagler grew up playing [[baseball]], [[American football|football]] and basketball. He played basketball at [[Duluth High School]] in [[Duluth, Georgia]].<ref name="werner">{{cite web |last1=Werner |first1=John |title=Adam Flagler flying high for unbeaten No. 2 Baylor Bears |url=https://wacotrib.com/sports/college/baylor/adam-flagler-flying-high-for-unbeaten-no-2-baylor-bears/article_a59a5b82-626f-11eb-818a-e3ecc236796b.html |work=[[Waco Tribune-Herald]] |access-date=April 5, 2021 |date=January 29, 2021}}</ref> Flagler left as the school's all-time leader in points (1,300) and three-pointers (227).<ref>{{cite web |last1=Woods |first1=David |title=Big South freshman of the year considers transfer to Butler |url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/college/butler/2019/05/02/butler-basketball-race-presbyterian-transfer-adam-flagler/3652929002/ |work=[[The Indianapolis Star]] |access-date=April 5, 2021 |date=May 2, 2019}}</ref> He was a two-time all-county selection.<ref name=werner/> He committed to playing college basketball for [[Presbyterian Blue Hose men's basketball|Presbyterian]], the only [[NCAA Division I]] program to offer him a scholarship.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Goodman |first1=Jeff |title=Adam Flagler's Path to Waco / How Baylor Was Built |url=https://watchstadium.com/adam-flaglers-path-to-waco/ |work=[[Stadium (sports network)|Stadium]] |access-date=April 5, 2021 |date=February 23, 2021}}</ref>

==College career==
On November 19, 2018, Flagler scored a career-high 29 points, making seven three-pointers, in an 80–65 loss to [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Duluth's Adam Flagler hits seven 3-pointers for Presbyterian against No. 17 UCLA |url=https://www.gwinnettdailypost.com/sports/duluth-s-adam-flagler-hits-seven-3-pointers-for-presbyterian-against-no-17-ucla/article_51358558-aac7-57aa-9d28-a7d216814a18.html |work=[[Gwinnett Daily Post]] |access-date=April 5, 2021 |date=November 20, 2018}}</ref> As a freshman at Presbyterian, he averaged 15.9 points and 3.4 rebounds per game, scoring the most points by a freshman in program Division I history. Flagler earned [[Big South]] Freshman of the Year honors and was a five-time Big South Freshman of the Week, a conference record.<ref>{{cite web |title=Duluth grad Adam Flagler makes commitment to Baylor men's basketball program |url=https://www.gwinnettdailypost.com/sports/duluth-grad-adam-flagler-makes-commitment-to-baylor-mens-basketball-program/article_b263a4f2-70f6-11e9-8af9-f337987b0fbf.html |work=[[Gwinnett Daily Post]] |access-date=April 5, 2021 |date=May 7, 2019}}</ref> After the offseason departure of head coach [[Dustin Kerns]], he transferred to [[Baylor Bears men's basketball|Baylor]] and sat out for one year due to transfer rules. During his [[redshirt (college sports)|redshirt]] year, Flagler improved his all-around game by practicing against [[Jared Butler]], [[Davion Mitchell]] and [[MaCio Teague]]. As a sophomore in [[2020–21 Baylor Bears basketball team|2021]], he assumed a [[sixth man]] role for Baylor, which finished with a 28–2 record and won the first [[2021 NCAA Division I men's basketball championship game|National championship]] in school history.<ref name=werner/> Flagler averaged 9.1 points, 2.3 rebounds, and 1.4 assists per game.<ref>{{cite news |last1=O'Neil |first1=Dana |title=Ten thoughts on Baylor's 10 scholarship players as Scott Drew embarks on his title defense |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/2578912/2021/05/11/ten-thoughts-on-baylors-10-scholarship-players-as-scott-drew-embarks-on-his-title-defense/ |access-date=June 21, 2021 |work=[[The Athletic]] |date=May 11, 2021}}</ref> On February 19, 2022, he was ruled out due to a knee injury.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Schultz |first1=Nick |title=Baylor announces two more key injuries ahead of TCU matchup |url=https://www.on3.com/college/baylor-bears/news/baylor-announces-two-more-key-injuries-ahead-of-tcu-matchup-lj-cryer-aj-flagler/ |access-date=February 21, 2022 |website=On3.com |date=February 19, 2022}}</ref> Flagler was named to the Second Team All-[[Big 12]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Kelly |first1=Eric |title=James Akinjo and Adam Flagler make AP All-Big 12 teams |url=https://www.fox44news.com/sports/baylor/james-akinjo-and-adam-flagler-make-ap-all-big-12-teams/ |access-date=March 10, 2022 |work=Fox 44 News |date=March 8, 2022}}</ref> He averaged 13.8 points and 3.0 assists per game. Following the season, Flagler declared for the [[2022 NBA draft]], before returning to Baylor.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Allen |first1=Jack |title=Baylor's Flagler declares for NBA Draft |url=https://www.kxxv.com/sports/baylor-bears/baylors-flagler-declares-for-nba-draft |access-date=March 6, 2023 |work=KXXV |date=April 21, 2022}}</ref> As a senior, he was named to the First Team All-Big 12.<ref>{{cite news |title=Flagler named first-team all-Big 12 |url=https://wacotrib.com/sports/college/baylor/flagler-named-first-team-all-big-12/article_99f8d02c-bba2-11ed-af41-6bdce25ad8ae.html |access-date=March 6, 2023 |work=[[Waco Tribune-Herald]] |date=March 5, 2023}}</ref> After the 2023 season, Flagler declared for the NBA draft once again.

==Professional career==
===Oklahoma City Thunder / Blue (2023–2025)===
After going undrafted in the [[2023 NBA draft]], Flagler signed with the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] on October 19, 2023, but was waived the next day.<ref>{{cite web|first=Arthur|last=Hill|title=Thunder Sign, Waive Caleb McConnell, Adam Flagler|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2023/10/caleb-mcconnell-adam-flagler-sign-with-thunder.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=October 20, 2023|access-date=October 22, 2023}}</ref> On October 31, he joined the [[Oklahoma City Blue]].<ref>{{cite tweet|author=OKC BLUE|title=Let’s work 🫡 2023-24 #OKCBlue Training Camp Roster🔵|number=1719380343176716560|user=okcblue|date=October 31, 2023|access-date=November 21, 2023}}</ref> On February 12, 2024, Flagler signed a [[two-way contract]] with the Thunder.<ref>{{cite web |date=February 12, 2024 |title=Thunder Signs Adam Flagler to Two-Way Contract |url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/release-flagler-240212 |access-date=February 12, 2024 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> Despite not appearing in the [[2025 NBA playoffs]] due to his two-way contract, Flagler won his first [[List of NBA champions|NBA championship]] with the Thunder after they defeated the [[Indiana Pacers]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Photos: 2025 NBA Finals Game 7 {{!}} Oklahoma City Thunder |url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/photos/finalsgame7-250622 |access-date=2025-08-13 |website=nba.com}}</ref>
===Austin Spurs (2025–2026)===
On August 10, 2025, Flagler signed an [[Exhibit 10]] contract with the [[San Antonio Spurs]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Jeje |first=Gomez |date=2025-08-10 |title=Spurs sign guard Adam Flagler to training camp deal |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/article/spurs-sign-guard-adam-flagler-235131490.html |access-date=2025-08-13 |work=Yahoo Sports}}</ref> He was waived by San Antonio prior to the start of the regular season on October 18.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Adams |first=Luke |date=October 19, 2025 |title=Spurs Waive Flagler, Umude, Potter; Biyombo Makes Team |url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2025/10/spurs-waive-flagler-umude-potter-biyombo-makes-team.html |access-date=2025-12-06 |work=Hoops Rumors}}</ref> For the [[2025–26 NBA G League season|2025–26 season]], he was added to the roster of the Spurs' G League affiliate, the [[Austin Spurs]].
===Sacramento / Stockton Kings (2026–present)===
On July 1, 2026, Flagler signed a two-way contract with the [[Sacramento Kings]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Kings Sign Adam Flagler To Two-Way Contract |url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2026/07/kings-adam-flagler-agree-to-two-way-contract.html |access-date=July 1, 2026 |work=Hoops Rumors}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Flagler's older brother, DuVaughn, played [[college football]] as a [[wide receiver]] at [[Gardner–Webb Runnin' Bulldogs football|Gardner–Webb]] and is an [[primary school|elementary school]] principal. Another older brother, Alex, played college basketball at [[Coker University|Coker College]] and [[Cumberland University]].<ref name=werner/>
